description: The golden corpus for the refresh-response.v2 wire contract: a successful refresh whose access token is the EdDSA access-token.v1 JWS. This manifest is the SINGLE inventory: every runner reads THIS file over THESE fixtures (G-70). `reject_by_client` documents are valid against the schema and refused by ParseRefreshResponse: the header and claims rules of access-token.v1 (the same ParseAccessToken), the token's sid against session_id, and expires_in against exp - iat. Tokens are synthetic: real header and payload segments, a signature segment that begins EXAMPLE.

accept.why: An EdDSA access-token.v1 JWS, 60 minutes, and the 7 day refresh credential.
expires_in is exp - iat of the token, not a constant: ten minutes.

reject.why: The v2 schema accepts only refresh-response.v2; a v1 version string is parsed by the v1 schema.
A lifetime of zero is not a token anyone can use.
Two segments: not a compact JWS.
An empty payload segment: not a compact JWS.
The user object is not part of this contract.
A dot is not in the credential alphabet: a refresh JWT cannot be presented here.
A header segment of nine characters: 4k+1 characters is no base64url.
A padded signature segment: base64url here is unpadded.
The standard-alphabet character + is not in the URL alphabet.
A line break inside a segment; a lenient decoder skips it.

reject_by_client.why: Header alg HS256: a symmetric algorithm is never this token's (access-token.v1 header).
Header typ JWT: the HS256 token's type, not at+jwt.
No kid: a verifier could not pick a key.
A jku member moves key selection out of the verifier's hands.
A duplicate member inside the decoded header is refused before any other check.
The token lives 3601 s: over the ceiling although expires_in is in range.
expires_in 600 for a token that lives 3600 s.
The token's sid names another session than session_id.
The header decodes to bytes that are not exactly one JSON object.
Schema `integer` admits 3600.0; clients refuse decimal-form tokens.
The header segment's last character carries non-zero trailing bits: the same bytes under a second spelling.
The payload segment's last character carries non-zero trailing bits.
The signature segment's last character carries non-zero trailing bits.
